subject: Microburst contingency credit & staggered true-up plan
messages:
From: Alice Morton <alice@brightcart.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com, wayne.li@brightcart.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected launch microburst — need short-window headroom and settlement options

Hi Sean,

We hit a sudden traffic microburst during our promotional push this morning and exhausted the headroom we'd planned. The stack remained stable but we incurred significant overrun charges and some throttling for a 45-minute window. Procurement asked me to get in touch to see what short-term protection you can offer (temporary quota, grace credits, or a blended true-up) while we finalize our committed tier.

Quick facts:
- Incident window: 2027-05-18 08:10–08:55 PT
- Estimated extra tokens: ~12M generation tokens
- Impact: 2% user error rate spike (retriable) and degraded latency for some vendor flows

Can we get a one-off mitigation and a path to avoid this on our next campaign? We have a signed LOI and are on a contract discussion track (BRG-4567).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call.

— Alice
Alice Morton
Head of Platform, BrightCart
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Alice Morton <alice@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected launch microburst — need short-window headroom and settlement options

Hi Alice — sorry to hear about the spike and glad the stack stayed functional. Thanks for the incident details; that helps a lot.

Short answer: yes, we can put a temporary buffer in place and propose a staggered true-up so BrightCart doesn't get hit with the full overrun in one invoice. Proposed immediate actions:

1) Temporary headroom: enable an emergency +50% quota for a 72-hour window (manual lift). No change to your committed tier; this is to cover any follow-on bursts while you finish the rollout.

2) One-time mitigation credit: Redwood will apply a partial credit equal to 40% of estimated overrun charges for the 45-minute window as good-faith relief while we reconcile telemetry.

3) Staggered true-up: spread the remaining overrun charges over the next two monthly invoices (50%/50%) or convert to a short-term prepaid burst credit if you prefer cap-and-prepay.

I'll loop Karhtik (AE) and Laura (Finance) to finalize numbers and paperwork. If BrightCart prefers, we can push a short amendment to the LOI to codify the temporary headroom and the credit.

Would you be available for a 20-minute call today at 2:00 PM PT?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected launch microburst — need short-window headroom and settlement options

Quick pricing calc attached.

I ran a quick back-of-envelope based on their token estimate (~12M gen tokens):
- List overrun charge estimate: $1,080 (assuming $0.00009/token gen)
- 40% goodwill credit -> $432 credit
- Remaining to true up: $648 -> split 50/50 across next two invoices = $324/mo (or convert to a $648 prepaid burst credit).

If we enable a 72-hour emergency headroom we should also add a short note that future repeated microbursts will be reviewed for a permanent tier increase vs. additional one-offs. Recommend adding a clause in the LOI amendment.

Attachment: BrightCart_microburst_proposal.pdf (pricing calc + amendment draft)

— Karthik
From: Wayne Li <wayne.li@brightcart.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Alice Morton <alice@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected launch microburst — need short-window headroom and settlement options

Thanks for the quick turnaround. The proposed structure sounds reasonable. A couple of asks from procurement/finance perspective:

- Can the 40% goodwill credit be applied before tax/fees are calculated (i.e., reduce the billed amount)?
- We prefer the staggered true-up spread over three invoices instead of two to smooth cashflow for this quarter.
- Please confirm the emergency +50% quota will be retroactive to the incident window so we don't get an extra spike billed for any backfilled traffic.

If you can confirm those items we can sign the LOI amendment and push the payment path through procurement today.

Wayne Li
CFO, BrightCart
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Wayne Li <wayne.li@brightcart.com>, Alice Morton <alice@brightcart.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected launch microburst — need short-window headroom and settlement options

Wayne — thanks, and appreciated the preference notes. Confirmations below: 

- Credit application: The 40% goodwill credit will be applied to the invoiced overrun amount prior to any applicable taxes and fees — it will reduce the billed subtotal.
- Staggered schedule: We can spread the remaining balance across three equal invoices (33%/33%/34%) to match your cashflow ask.
- Retroactive headroom: We'll mark the emergency +50% quota as effective for the incident window (2027-05-18 08:10–08:55 PT) and remove related overrun assessments for that interval.

Next steps: I attached the LOI amendment with the three bullet points captured and a DocuSign link for signature. Once we have the signed amendment, we'll apply the credit and issue the adjusted invoices per the schedule.

Attachments: BrightCart_microburst_proposal.pdf, LOI_amendment_BRG-4567.docx
DocuSign: https://docusign.redwood.com/doc/AA12-BRG4567
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/BRG-4567

If BrightCart signs today we can apply the credit and adjusted invoicing before the next billing run.

— Laura Bennett
Senior Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
